blocks.content: The recommendations of TRAI are not binding upon the Central Government.

items: TRAI's recommendations regarding telecom service licensing are advisory in nature and not binding on the Government.
Dispute adjudication powers were completely moved from TRAI to TDSAT under the 2000 Amendment Act.
Members hold office for a term of 3 years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI was established under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997, to regulate telecommunication services.
The 2000 Amendment separated adjudicatory functions from TRAI and created the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT).
TRAI consists of a Chairperson, up to two full-time members, and up to two part-time members appointed by the Central Government.
TRAI holds mandatory powers to fix and revise tariffs for telecommunication services in India.
TRAI's recommendations on spectrum management and telecom licensing are advisory and not binding on the Central Government.
